article.title: China Recovers Long March 10B Booster With Net Capture at Sea, Becoming Second Nation to Land an Orbital-Class Rocket
article.summary: CASC's new Long March 10B caught its own booster in a sea-based net on its maiden flight July 10, joining SpaceX and Blue Origin as the only operators to recover an orbital-class rocket stage.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) launched the new Long March 10B rocket on its maiden flight from the Hainan Commercial Space Launch Site at 12:15 a.m. Eastern (0415 UTC) on July 10, 2026, and recovered the vehicle's first stage using a net-based capture system on a ship at sea, [according to SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). The successful recovery sees CASC join SpaceX and Blue Origin as the only organizations to have recovered an orbital-class booster, [SpaceNews reported](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/), and CASC called it the country's first successful controlled recovery of a launch vehicle and the world's first net-based recovery of a launch vehicle, [according to Scientific American](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chinas-long-march-10b-rocket-successfully-launches-and-lands-in-a-global-spaceflight-milestone/).

## What We Know

The Long March 10B is a five-meter-diameter, two-stage rocket measuring 63 meters long with a liftoff mass of 760,000 kilograms, [SpaceNews reported](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). Its first stage is powered by seven YF-100K kerosene-liquid oxygen engines producing a combined 890 tons of thrust, [SpaceNews reported](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). The second stage uses a single liquid oxygen-methane engine, [according to Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202607/1365624.shtml). In its reusable configuration the rocket can lift 16,000 kilograms to low Earth orbit, [SpaceNews reported](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). On its debut flight, the rocket carried an undisclosed satellite payload into orbit, [per SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/).

Roughly six minutes after the first and second stages separated, the booster made a controlled, powered descent and was caught by hooks engaging a tensioned net strung across the deck of a recovery ship, the Linghang Zhe, or "navigator," [according to SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). The first stage made a vertical return before it was successfully recovered by the offshore platform, [Global Times reported](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202607/1365622.shtml). The system uses a flexible net with hydraulic damping, eliminating the need for the deployable landing legs used on other reusable rockets, [SpaceNews reported](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/), and Scientific American similarly described the booster deploying "four comparatively lightweight 'landing hooks'" to engage the [novel net-based recovery system](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chinas-long-march-10b-rocket-successfully-launches-and-lands-in-a-global-spaceflight-milestone/). The recovery ship measures 144 meters by 50 meters with a full-load displacement of 25,000 tonnes and was delivered by the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology (CALT) in November 2025, [according to Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20260710/3ad9cf3d515642f0ba3922040b9a28c6/c.html).

CASC's Chen Muye said, "Net-based recovery simplifies the onboard structure, reduces weight, and boosts payload capacity," [Xinhua reported](https://english.news.cn/20260710/3ad9cf3d515642f0ba3922040b9a28c6/c.html). CASC's Xu Xuelei described the recovery platform's design, saying, "The platform's massive tower structure is anchored to the deck by four large supports," [per Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20260710/3ad9cf3d515642f0ba3922040b9a28c6/c.html). Sun Zhenlian, a technical expert at the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology, characterized the capture mechanism as "like powerful hands firmly grasping the rocket," [Global Times reported](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202607/1365624.shtml).

CASC said it intends to reuse the recovered first stage on another flight before the end of the year, [according to SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/), a plan corroborated by Global Times, which reported a [reused first-stage flight test is expected by the end of 2026](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202607/1365624.shtml). Long Lehao, an expert at the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said, "The Long March-10A, 10B and 10C will collectively form the backbone of China's space transportation system," [Xinhua reported](https://english.news.cn/20260710/3ad9cf3d515642f0ba3922040b9a28c6/c.html). China is also developing a larger Long March 10C variant using an all liquid oxygen-methane configuration to support satellite-constellation and crewed missions, [according to Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202607/1365624.shtml). Scientific American reported that the flight validated the related Long March 10A design, which is intended to launch the Mengzhou crew spacecraft supporting China's goal of [landing astronauts on the lunar surface before 2030](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chinas-long-march-10b-rocket-successfully-launches-and-lands-in-a-global-spaceflight-milestone/).

The recovery is also notable because it succeeded on the rocket's first attempt. Scientific American noted that no other organization has achieved [a flawless first-stage booster recovery on a vehicle's inaugural launch](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chinas-long-march-10b-rocket-successfully-launches-and-lands-in-a-global-spaceflight-milestone/). Global Times likewise framed the milestone as making China [the second country to master vertical rocket recovery technology](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202607/1365624.shtml).

The launch follows China's June 1 debut of the reusable Long March 12B, [as previously reported](/article/2026-06/06-china-debuts-reusable-long-march-12b-in-a-surprise-launch-delivering-qianfan-satellites-without-advance-airspace-notice), part of a broader push by CASC and other Chinese launch providers to bring reusable rocket families into commercial service.

## What We Don't Know

CASC has not disclosed the purpose or specifications of the satellite carried on the Long March 10B's debut flight, [per SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). CASC has not specified an exact date for the planned reflight of the recovered booster beyond a general end-of-2026 target, [according to SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/).
